Equinix reported 1.26 billion dollars in quarterly capital expenditure for the quarter ending March 2026, roughly double its 617 million dollar quarter in late 2023, but still the second smallest capex figure among the eight builders tracked here.

Equinix's spending climbed in almost every reported quarter across the series, from 617 million to 648 million to 707 million to 724 million to 750 million to 989 million to 1.14 billion to 1.26 billion, a steady, unbroken upward path rather than a single step change. That pattern separates it from CoreWeave's spike or Alphabet's acceleration elsewhere in this peer set, and it reads as sustained, incremental capacity building rather than a rushed response to a single opportunity.

Against its seven peers, Equinix's 1.26 billion dollars is a fraction of Amazon's 54.2 billion or Alphabet's 35.7 billion, and it sits just above only Digital Realty's 870 million. A single SEC filing from July 2026 disclosing a new financial obligation is the only recent filing activity recorded for the company, far less than CoreWeave's six filings in the same year, which suggests Equinix is financing its buildout through fewer, larger transactions rather than a continuous stream of new agreements.
